A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniMLVG and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. Their methods, experiments, equations, tables and figures can be matched. Appendix figures on PDF pages 13–25 are visually identical.

before.justification: V2 reports original nuScenes generation and perception results, ablation experiments, dataset annotation statistics and qualitative generation examples, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical investigations and reports revised generation and ablation scores in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The backbone, temporal and cross-view modules, four training tasks, losses, camera-ray conditioning and three training stages are retained. Expanded ray-encoding notation and training explanations clarify operations already described in v2, including Supplementary Section 6; they do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenDV-Youtube, nuScenes, Waymo and Argoverse2. Generation with and without reference frames, weather editing and generation from CARLA conditions are retained, including the same supplementary examples.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DriveGAN, DriveDreamer, MagicDrive, Drive-WM, DriveDreamer-2, DreamForge, DiVE and Oracle, with unchanged comparator scores. The condition-ablation comparator configurations also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 in v2 specifies FID on 10,000 sampled images from 900 sixteen-frame videos. V3 instead says the 900 videos support both FID and FVD, without specifying FID frame sampling. This leaves unclear whether sampling changed or its description was shortened. Newly stated ablation initialization and training-stage details do not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The same conditioning, dataset, training-stage and task-ratio ablations remain, but their quantitative evidence is revised. For example, Table 2 replaces the near-tied camera-ray versus implicit-camera FIDs of 11.71 versus 11.74 with 6.78 versus 8.74. No new robustness tests, analysis questions or qualitative case studies are added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The descriptive dataset statistics in Figure 8 are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces UniMLVG's FID/FVD of 8.8/60.1 with 5.8/36.1, changing its reported FVD rank from second to first. Tables 2–5 revise most ablation scores; for example, Stage II FVD changes from 64.44 to 44.43. Perception scores and qualitative examples remain unchanged. These are substantial result replacements, but uncertain FID sampling prevents treating them as verified same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The flow losses, camera-ray construction and gated feature-fusion mathematics are retained. V3 expands the Fourier encoding into componentwise encoding and concatenation, clarifying the ray-origin and direction encoding already described in v2. No new theoretical result, assumption or proof appears.

C1.justification: The headline FID advantage changes from 21.4% to 48.2%. The headline FVD advantage becomes 35.2% over DriveDreamer-2, replacing 36.5% over DiVE and the previously reported second-place FVD standing. The method's claimed capabilities and contribution scope otherwise remain stable; explicit ray modeling was already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces 'zero-shot generalizability' with 'cross-distribution transfer' for weather editing and removes the explanation about addressing scarce corner cases through simulation. Its performance attribution also shifts from emphasizing the pretrained image backbone to emphasizing training strategies and explicit perspective modeling.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies that Stage III typically takes one or two epochs, describes Stage II and Stage I initialization as the default ablation setup, and mentions view masking for differing viewpoint counts. Conversely, the explicit 10,000-image FID sampling detail is removed. Hardware, optimizer settings, inference settings and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the distinction from DriveDreamer-2 to emphasize IP and IG beyond its VP and VG tasks; Section 3.4 explicitly contrasts all-video training with image-then-video training. No distinct cited work is added: v3 references 40 and 41 duplicate the Scene Representation Transformer paper already cited in v2.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and selected method and experimental passages are rewritten or expanded. Multi-dataset discussion moves before multi-condition discussion, terminology is refined, and equations gain numbering. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves above the abstract. Figure 2 is redrawn and moves from PDF page 3 to page 4, with labeled noisy/reference latents and reorganized condition inputs. Figure 3's caption is shortened. Table structures and supplementary figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 clarifies ray encoding and training details, uses more careful weather-transfer wording, and makes the multi-dataset percentage consistent with Table 3. However, extensive score replacements lack a clear explanation of their source, while the explicit FID sampling rule disappears. These documentation gains and unresolved evaluation comparability prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
